title: Samba and Bossa Nova: Adverbs that Show Your View

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *lamentablemente*, *en realidad*, *en rigor*, *precisamente*, *apenas* and other adverbs from B2 Unit 1. They show how you stand towards a fact, or point at the exact word. Writing about music uses them to correct a common idea (*en realidad*) or to pin down a detail (*precisamente*). Here they work on samba and bossa nova.

sections.title: Stance and focus adverbs in Brazilian music
rows: En realidad, la bossa nova no nació en una favela, sino en apartamentos de Copacabana e Ipanema.
*en realidad* corrects what people may assume
Precisamente en los morros nacieron muchas escuelas de samba.
*precisamente* points at the place: exactly there
Lamentablemente, la dictadura obligó a algunos músicos a salir del país.
El disco, en rigor, salió en 1959, aunque la canción se grabó en 1958.
*en rigor* gives the exact, technical truth

items.spanish: En realidad, la bossa nova toma ideas de la samba.
items.english: In fact, bossa nova takes ideas from samba.

items.spanish: Gilberto cantaba casi susurrando; apenas levantaba la voz.
items.english: Gilberto sang almost whispering; he hardly raised his voice.

items.spanish: Fue precisamente en 1964 cuando los militares tomaron el poder.
items.english: It was exactly in 1964 that the military took power.

sections.content: Use the comma test from B2 Unit 1: if you can put commas round the adverb, it comments on the whole sentence (*En realidad, ...*). *Precisamente* and *apenas* sit right before the word they point at, with no commas. Use only one stance adverb per sentence.
